description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Σαρακήνικο στη Μήλο.
description.en: A lunar landscape of brilliant white volcanic rock — one of the most photographed beaches in the Aegean.

about:
The white rock of Sarakiniko is soft volcanic ash and pumice, worn by wind and sea into smooth ridges and hollows. In the middle, a narrow inlet runs inland. Swimmers jump into it from the ledges, and there is a small patch of sand at its head. Most people simply lay their towels on the rock.

There is no shade, no sunbeds and no taverna, so bring water and a hat: the white rock reflects the sun and gets very hot by midday. The beach faces north and takes the full force of the meltemi. On windy days the sea in the inlet can be rough and swimming is not safe. Come early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when the light is softer and the crowds have thinned.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Φυροπόταμος στη Μήλο.
description.en: A picturesque bay with crystal clear waters and traditional syrmata boathouses lining the shore.

about:
Firopotamos is a small, sheltered cove on the north coast, a short drive from Plaka. A row of syrmata, the traditional boathouses of Milos, lines one side of the water, and a tiny whitewashed chapel stands on the rocks at the mouth of the bay. The beach is a short strip of sand, and the water is shallow and very clear, which makes it easy for children.

There are a few sunbeds but little else, so bring water and snacks. Parking is limited and fills up by late morning in July and August. The cove faces north, so when the meltemi blows the water can get choppy. On calm days it is one of the prettiest places to swim on this side of the island.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Τσιγκράδο στη Μήλο.
description.en: A hidden gem reached by descending a rope through a narrow cliff crevice, with dazzling turquoise water below.

about:
Tsigrado is a tiny cove of pale sand and turquoise water on the south coast, closed in by high cliffs and right next to Firiplaka. The only way down is through a narrow gully in the cliff, using a rope and a wooden ladder. The climb is short but steep. It is not for small children or anyone unsteady on their feet, and it is best done with your hands free, so leave bulky bags in the car.

The cove is small and fills up quickly in high season. Arrive early or late in the day. The cliffs give some shade, and the rocks on either side are good for snorkelling. Facing south, Tsigrado is sheltered from the meltemi and the water is usually calm.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Φυριπλάκα στη Μήλο.
description.en: A long sandy beach on the south coast, sheltered from the meltemi winds and ideal throughout the summer.

about:
Firiplaka is one of the longest and most popular beaches on Milos: a wide sweep of sand on the south coast, backed by cliffs in shades of white, red and grey. A tall rock stands on the sand and makes an easy landmark. One part of the beach has sunbeds and a beach bar, and the rest is free, with plenty of room to spread out even in August.

The beach faces south and is well sheltered from the meltemi. That makes it a good choice on windy days, when the north coast is rough. The water stays shallow near the shore, so it suits families. Tsigrado is a few minutes' walk to the east, if you want to combine the two.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Παλαιοχώρι στη Μήλο.
description.en: A unique geothermal beach where volcanic heat warms the sand from below — and the water from beneath the surface.

about:
Paleochori is really three beaches in one, separated by rocks on the south coast. It is known for its volcanic activity. In places the sand is hot to the touch, and warm water and gas bubble up from the seabed near the shore. The cliffs behind the beach are streaked red, yellow and white by the minerals in the rock.

The main beach is organised, with sunbeds, beach bars and tavernas. One of them, Sirocco, cooks food buried in the hot volcanic sand. The coves at either end are quieter. Paleochori faces south, so it is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm in summer, and the sand slopes gently into the water.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Προβατάς στη Μήλο.
description.en: A family-friendly beach with calm shallow water, full facilities, and easy road access on the south coast.

about:
Provatas is a wide sandy beach on the south coast, set between headlands of red and ochre volcanic rock. The sand is fine and the water stays shallow far out, which makes it one of the easiest beaches on the island for families with small children. It is reached by a paved road from Adamas, with parking close to the sand.

There are sunbeds, a beach bar and tavernas nearby, as well as rooms to rent if you want to stay by the sea. Facing south, Provatas is sheltered from the meltemi and stays calm on most summer days. Agios Sostis, a quieter beach with no facilities, is just to the west.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Παπαφράγκας στη Μήλο.
description.en: A series of narrow sea caves carved into the volcanic cliffs — magical for swimming.

about:
Papafragas is not a beach in the usual sense. It is a narrow sea inlet: a channel of turquoise water between high white cliffs on the north coast, with a tiny patch of sand at its end. A path and rough steps lead down from the road. From the top you can see the arch where the inlet meets the open sea. It is said to have been a hiding place for pirate boats.

The ruins of ancient Phylakopi, one of the oldest settlements in the Cyclades, are a short walk away. There are no facilities. Facing north, Papafragas is exposed to the meltemi. On windy days waves surge through the channel and swimming can be dangerous, so come on a calm morning.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Κλέφτικο στη Μήλο.
description.en: The crown jewel of Milos — dramatic sea caves and arches on the southwest tip, accessible only by boat.

about:
On the south-west tip of Milos, tall white rocks rise straight out of the sea, cut through with caves, arches and tunnels that you can swim or paddle into. The name comes from the kleftes, the pirates who are said to have hidden their ships among the rocks. There is no road, so Kleftiko can only be reached by sea.

Most people come on a day boat trip from Adamas. These usually stop at Kleftiko for a swim and continue to other caves along the south-west coast, such as Sikia. Sailing trips and sea kayak tours also go there. The water is deep and very clear, ideal for snorkelling. Boat trips can be cancelled on very windy days, so keep your plans flexible.

description.el: Μεγάλη αμμουδιά στη νότια ακτή, με ρηχά καθαρά νερά, ξαπλώστρες και ταβέρνες κοντά. Ιδανική για οικογένειες.
description.en: A long sandy beach on the south coast with shallow, clear water, sunbeds and tavernas nearby. Ideal for families.

about:
Agia Kyriaki is a long sandy beach on the south coast, named after a small chapel nearby. The sand is fine and the water is shallow and clear. The cliffs behind it have the warm colours of the volcanic rock found all along this coast. It is a good all-round beach: organised, with sunbeds, a beach bar and tavernas, but long enough to find a quieter spot.

The road from Adamas is paved and there is parking near the sand. Facing south, Agia Kyriaki is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm. That makes it a reliable choice for families on windy days. Paleochori and Deep Blue Beach are a short drive to the east.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Γέροντας στη Μήλο.
description.en: A remote beach with striking red and orange volcanic cliffs — few crowds and spectacular scenery.

about:
Gerontas is a remote pebble beach in the south-west of Milos, at the end of a long dirt track. The cliffs around it are among the most colourful on the island, in deep red, orange and yellow, and the sea in front is a clean, bright blue. Getting there takes some effort, so it is rarely busy, even in August.

There are no facilities and no natural shade, so bring water, food and an umbrella. The track is rough in places. Drive slowly, or use a four-wheel drive if you have one. The beach faces south-west and is sheltered from the meltemi on most days.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Triades Beach στη Μήλο.
description.en: A long sandy beach on the northwest coast, naturally beautiful and unspoiled, with no facilities.

about:
Triades is a long, wild sandy beach on the west coast of Milos, in the quiet western half of the island where most roads are dirt. There are no sunbeds and no taverna, and often only a handful of people. The view opens to the west, which makes it a fine place to stay for the sunset.

Bring water, food and shade, and allow time for the drive. The last stretch is unpaved and can be rough after winter. The beach faces west, so it is partly exposed to the meltemi and can get waves on windy days. Ammoudaraki is just to the south if you want to explore further.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Λιμνοθάλασσα Ριβάρι στη Μήλο.
description.en: A stunning natural lagoon where warm shallow water is separated from the open sea by a sand strip.

about:
Rivari is a shallow saltwater lagoon on the western side of Milos Bay, separated from the sea by a narrow strip of sand. The water in the lagoon is calm and shallow and warms up quickly. The beach on the sea side looks out across the bay. It is a quiet, natural spot with no facilities.

The lagoon is a small wetland, used by birds through the year, so tread lightly and take all rubbish with you. There is no shade, so bring your own. Because it lies inside the bay, the sea here is usually gentler than on the open coast.

description.el: Θαλάσσια σπηλιά στη νοτιοδυτική ακτή με κατεστραμμένη οροφή, από την οποία το φως πέφτει στα τιρκουάζ νερά. Προσβάσιμη μόνο με σκάφος ή καγιάκ.
description.en: A sea cave on the south-west coast with a collapsed roof that lets sunlight fall onto turquoise water. Reachable only by boat or kayak.

about:
Sikia is a large sea cave on the south-west coast, a short way along from Kleftiko. Part of its roof has collapsed, and sunlight falls straight down through the opening onto the water inside, turning it a bright, glowing turquoise. There is no beach and no way to get there by land.

Sikia is a stop on many boat trips around the south-west coast, often on the same day as Kleftiko, and sea kayak tours paddle inside. The light in the cave is best around midday, when the sun is high and shines straight through the roof. Trips depend on the sea, and on very windy days boats may skip it.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Plathiena στη Μήλο.
description.en: A long sandy beach near Plaka with good facilities and colourful volcanic cliffs.

about:
Plathiena is a sandy beach on the north coast, in a deep bay below Plaka. It is one of the closest beaches to the capital, with sunbeds and a taverna. The cliffs on either side are coloured by the volcanic rock, and the water is shallow and clear near the shore.

It is easy to pair a swim here with an evening in Plaka and the sunset from the Kastro, a short drive up the hill. Plathiena faces north, so it gets waves when the meltemi blows. On calm days it is one of the nicest beaches on this side of the island, and it is a good one for children.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Θειορυχειο στη Μήλο.
description.en: A historic beach featuring abandoned sulfur mines and rusted machinery against colourful cliffs.

about:
Thiorichia is a pebble beach on the east coast, at the site of the old sulphur mines of Milos. Sulphur was mined here until the middle of the 20th century. The abandoned buildings, rails and rusted machinery still stand above the beach, slowly being taken back by the landscape. The cliffs around them are stained yellow and orange by the sulphur.

The way in is a long, rough dirt road, best done in a four-wheel drive or partly on foot. There are no facilities, so bring everything you need. Take care around the ruins: the buildings are unstable and best seen from outside. Facing east, the beach is partly sheltered from the meltemi.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Αχιβαδόλιμνη στη Μήλο.
description.en: A large, popular beach with sandy bottom, crystal clear waters and ideal conditions for windsurfing.

about:
Achivadolimni is the longest beach on Milos, a wide strip of sand on the southern shore of Milos Bay, a short drive from Adamas. Its name means "clam lake", after the small salt lake behind the beach. The water is clear, with a sandy bottom that shelves gently. There are sunbeds in places and plenty of free space.

The beach faces north across the bay, so the meltemi blows straight onto it. That makes the water choppy on windy days, but it is also why Achivadolimni is the main windsurfing spot on the island. On calm mornings it is a peaceful, easy beach for families.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Άγιος Σώστης στη Μήλο.
description.en: A serene quiet beach with shallow waters, offering a peaceful escape from busier spots.

about:
Agios Sostis is a small sandy beach on the south coast, just west of Provatas. It has the same shallow, clear water and warm-coloured cliffs as its busier neighbour, but no sunbeds or beach bar. That makes it a good place to swim in peace, even in high season.

Bring your own shade and water. Tavernas, a beach bar and parking are a short distance away at Provatas. Facing south, Agios Sostis is well sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm, and the gentle slope into the water suits children.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Τρία Πηγάδια στη Μήλο.
description.en: A secluded, rugged beach favoured by those looking for privacy and untouched natural beauty.

about:
Tria Pigadia, meaning "three wells", is a secluded pebble beach on the east coast of Milos. It sits below rugged hills with hardly a building in sight. People come here for solitude: there are no sunbeds, no taverna and usually very few visitors. The water is clear and deepens quickly off the pebbles.

The approach is by dirt road, so drive slowly and check the track before taking an ordinary car down. Bring water, food and shade. Facing east, the beach is partly sheltered from the meltemi, though it can still get some swell. Kastanas and Kolympionas, two other quiet beaches, are close by.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Καστανάς στη Μήλο.
description.en: A striking beach with colourful volcanic pebbles set against dramatic high cliffs.

about:
Kastanas is a pebble beach on the east coast, at the foot of high cliffs. The pebbles come in a surprising range of colours, from white and grey to red and green, washed smooth by the sea. It is one of a string of quiet, wild beaches along this coast, with no facilities and few visitors.

The beach is reached by dirt road, so take it slowly. Bring water and shade, as the cliffs only give cover early in the day. Facing east, Kastanas is partly sheltered from the meltemi. Tria Pigadia is just to the south if you want to visit more than one beach.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Pollonia beach, Milos στη Μήλο.
description.en: A convenient family-friendly beach in the fishing village of Pollonia, close to cafes and tavernas.

about:
Pollonia Beach is the sandy beach in the fishing village of Pollonia, in the north-east of Milos, running along the bay next to the harbour. Its great advantage is convenience. Cafés, bakeries and some of the best fish tavernas on the island are a few steps away, and the shallow water suits young children. The boat to Kimolos leaves from the harbour nearby.

The bay faces east, which gives it some protection from the meltemi, though it can still be breezy. In high season, arrive early for a spot on the sand. Or stay into the evening, when the village fills up for dinner by the water.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Μανδράκια στη Μήλο.
description.en: A beautiful beach with clear blue waters, famous for the traditional colourful syrmata boathouses.

about:
Mandrakia is a tiny fishing hamlet on the north coast. A few colourful syrmata boathouses are built into the rock around a small, narrow inlet. There is no sandy beach: people swim off the rocks and the boat ramps, in clear blue water. It is one of the most photographed corners of Milos, especially in the late afternoon light.

The taverna above the water is the other reason to come. Parking is limited and the road down is narrow. Facing north, Mandrakia is exposed to the meltemi, and on windy days the inlet can be too rough for swimming. On a calm day, it is lovely for a quiet swim and a long lunch.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Αγγαθια στη Μήλο.
description.en: A tranquil lesser-known spot, ideal for those seeking privacy away from the crowds.

about:
Aggathia is a small pebble beach on the north-west coast of Milos, in the remote western half of the island. It sees few visitors, and that is its appeal: clear water, a wild coastline and room to yourself even in summer.

There are no facilities, so bring water, food and shade. The roads on this side of the island are mostly dirt, so allow extra time and drive carefully. The beach faces north-west and is exposed to the meltemi. It is best on calm days, when the sea is flat and very clear.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Αμμουδαρακι στη Μήλο.
description.en: A remote and peaceful beach featuring soft sand and beautiful natural surroundings.

about:
Ammoudaraki, meaning "little sand", is a remote sandy beach on the west coast of Milos, just south of Triades. Soft sand, clear water and low hills with no buildings make it feel far from the busy south coast. Visitors are few, even in high season.

There are no facilities, and the last part of the road is a dirt track, so bring everything you need and allow time for the drive. The beach faces west, with good sunset views. It is partly exposed to the meltemi, so the sea can be lively on windy days.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Kalamos στη Μήλο.
description.en: A beautiful beach with fine golden sand and deep clear blue waters, surrounded by volcanic scenery.

about:
Kalamos is a sandy beach on the south coast, a little east of Firiplaka and Tsigrado. The golden sand is surrounded by volcanic scenery, and the water is clear and deepens fairly quickly, which suits confident swimmers. It is much quieter than its famous neighbours.

There are no facilities, so bring water and shade. The beach is reached by dirt road, and the last part may need to be done on foot. Facing south, Kalamos is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm in summer.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Άγιος Ιωάννης στη Μήλο.
description.en: A long wild and mostly secluded beach on the west side of the island.

about:
Agios Ioannis Beach is a long, wild beach on the west coast of Milos, in the remote south-western part of the island. It takes its name from the monastery of Agios Ioannis Siderianos nearby. The beach is mostly empty, with open views to the west that make it a fine place for the sunset.

There are no facilities. The drive is long, and part of it is on dirt roads, so bring water, food and shade, and leave plenty of time to get back before dark. Facing west, the beach is partly exposed to the meltemi and can get waves on windy days.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Κήπος στη Μήλο.
description.en: A small serene beach known for its clear waters and proximity to traditional fish tavernas.

about:
Kipos is a small pebble beach on the south coast. Its clear, shallow water makes it a calm, easy place to swim. It is quieter than the big sandy beaches further east, and a taverna is nearby for lunch.

Bring your own shade, as there is little cover on the beach. Facing south, Kipos is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm in summer. Psathi, another quiet beach, is a short distance to the west if you want to explore this stretch of coast.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία DeepBlue Beach στη Μήλο.
description.en: A hidden cove with incredibly deep blue waters, offering a sense of isolation and raw beauty.

about:
Deep Blue Beach is a small hidden cove on the south coast, between Agia Kyriaki and Paleochori. Volcanic rock surrounds the water, which drops off quickly to a deep, intense blue: as the name says, this is a place for swimming and snorkelling rather than paddling.

There are no facilities, and the way down is over rock, so wear proper shoes. Sunbeds, tavernas and parking are a short drive away at Agia Kyriaki and Paleochori. Facing south, the cove is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Ψαθί στη Μήλο.
description.en: A lovely quiet beach with a calm atmosphere, often visited for a peaceful swim.

about:
Psathi is a quiet sandy beach on the south coast, west of Kipos. The atmosphere is calm and the water is shallow and clear, which makes it a good place for an unhurried swim away from the busier beaches.

There are no facilities, so bring water and shade. Facing south, Psathi is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm in summer. It is a good choice on windy days, when the north coast is rough.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Κολυμπιώνας στη Μήλο.
description.en: A rugged non-organised beach offering a wild landscape for nature lovers.

about:
Kolympionas is a rugged pebble beach on the east coast of Milos. It is not organised, and the wild, empty landscape around it is the main attraction. The water is clear and the setting feels a long way from the busy beaches of the south coast.

There are no facilities, and the road in is a dirt track, so bring everything you need and drive slowly. Facing east, the beach is partly sheltered from the meltemi. Tria Pigadia and Kastanas, two other quiet beaches, are close by to the north.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Βούδια στη Μήλο.
description.en: A unique beach with industrial history and proximity to old mines — a different side of Milos.

about:
Voudia is a pebble beach on the east coast, in the part of Milos still shaped by mining. Bentonite and perlite are extracted from the hills nearby, and the bay has a loading quay for ships carrying the minerals. It shows a working side of the island that most visitors never see.

The beach itself is open and quiet, with clear water and no facilities. Bring water and shade. Pollonia, with tavernas and cafés, is a short drive to the north. Facing east, Voudia is partly sheltered from the meltemi.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Πάχαινα στη Μήλο.
description.en: A lovely sandy beach with interesting rock formations and views of the Glaronisia islets.

about:
Pachaina is a small sandy beach on the north coast, between Sarakiniko and Pollonia. It has unusual rock formations and views out to the Glaronisia, the islets off this coast made of tall columns of volcanic rock. There is parking but no other facilities, and it is usually quiet.

Facing north, Pachaina takes the full meltemi, so the sea can be rough on windy days. It is best on calm mornings, when the water is clear and still. Papafragas is a short drive to the east.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Αλογομάντρα στη Μήλο.
description.en: A beach enclosed by high vertical rocks, creating a natural harbour and unique swimming experience.

about:
Alogomandra is a small pebble cove on the north coast, closed in by high vertical rocks that form a kind of natural harbour. The narrow entrance keeps the water inside calm when the sea is not too rough, and the rocks make it interesting for snorkelling. They also give some shade at certain times of day.

There is parking nearby but no other facilities. Facing north, the cove is exposed to the meltemi. On strong wind days, waves can push in through the entrance, so check the forecast before you go.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Μύτικας στη Μήλο.
description.en: A small scenic beach with traditional boat houses, popular for its clear waters.

about:
Mytakas is a small pebble beach on the north coast, close to Sarakiniko. A few traditional syrmata boathouses sit by the water, and the sea is shallow and very clear. There are a few sunbeds and parking, and it is usually much quieter than its famous neighbour.

Facing north, Mytakas is exposed to the meltemi, so on windy days the water can get rough. On calm days it is a good place to swim after a visit to Sarakiniko.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Νεροδάφνη στη Μήλο.
description.en: A secluded natural spot perfect for those who enjoy pristine environments.

about:
Nerodafni is a small, secluded pebble beach near the northern tip of Milos, north of Plathiena. The surroundings are untouched and the water is clear. It suits people who want a quiet swim away from the organised beaches.

There is parking but no other facilities, so bring water and shade. The beach faces north-west and is exposed to the meltemi. It is best on calm days.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Κλήμα στη Μήλο.
description.en: A unique beach at the famous settlement of Klima, known for the multi-coloured traditional syrmata.

about:
Klima is the best-known fishing village on Milos. Its colourful syrmata, boathouses with a garage for the boat at sea level and living quarters above, line the shore of Milos Bay for a few hundred metres. There is no real beach: people swim off the rocks and the boat ramps in front of the houses.

The village sits below Tripiti, the ancient theatre and the Catacombs, so it is easy to combine a swim with sightseeing. Parking is at the top of the village, and the lane along the water is best explored on foot. Facing south-east into the bay, Klima is sheltered from the meltemi, and there is a fish taverna by the water.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Παπικινού στη Μήλο.
description.en: A long tree-lined sandy beach near Adamas, offering plenty of shade and access to local tavernas.

about:
Papikinou is a long sandy beach on Milos Bay, just east of Adamas and within walking distance of the port. Trees line the back of the beach and give welcome shade, and the water is shallow and calm. With sunbeds, tavernas and cafés along the road behind, it is the most convenient beach if you are staying in Adamas.

Because it lies inside the bay, Papikinou is sheltered from the worst of the meltemi. Its west-facing outlook makes it a pleasant place for a late swim and the sunset over the bay.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Άγιος Δημήτριος στη Μήλο.
description.en: A quiet beach named after the local chapel, offering a peaceful setting and shallow waters.

about:
Agios Dimitrios is a quiet sandy beach on the western shore of Milos Bay, named after the small chapel nearby. Across the water from Adamas, it is usually reached by boat. Few people make the trip, so it stays peaceful even in summer.

The water is shallow and calm, well suited to children. Facing east across the bay, the beach is sheltered from the meltemi. There are no facilities, so bring water, food and shade.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Καλογριές στη Μήλο.
description.en: A remote sandy beach on the north-west coast, usually reached by boat and almost always quiet.

about:
Kalogries is a remote sandy beach on the north-west coast of Milos, usually reached by boat. Because getting there is hard, it is one of the quietest beaches on the island. The setting is wild and empty, and the Aegean is a clear, deep blue.

The beach faces north-west and is exposed to the meltemi, so boats go there on calm days. There are no facilities, so bring water, food and shade.

description.el: Ανακαλύψτε την παραλία Παραλία Κροτιράκι στη Μήλο.
description.en: A small sandy beach on the south coast, reached by boat, with shallow water and very few visitors.

about:
Krotiraki is a small sandy beach on the south coast of Milos, west of Kipos, usually reached by boat. It sees very few visitors, so it is a good stop for a quiet swim on a boat trip along the south coast.

The water is shallow and clear. Facing south, the beach is sheltered from the meltemi and usually calm in summer. There are no facilities.
